doc.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002

title: Why the saxophone: Swiss Movement and Eddie Harris
summary: He wanted to be a drummer but switched after hearing Les McCann and Eddie Harris and Cannonball records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: What brought you to the saxophone? Was it your first instrument?

Yeah. Formally anyway. I really wanted to be a drummer, before the age of twelve. But I think what changed me to saxophone was hearing the record “Swiss Movement,” Les McCann and Eddie Harris. Because that was a big hit around 1969, 1970, and that was one of the records my father had and I gravitated toward that. And then with allowance money I started going out and buying a couple of Eddie Harris records and of course Cannonball Adderley’s “Country Preacher” was a big hit at the time. So all of those things, I said oh this is — I like the way this sounds. I like the way this feels.
Yeah. We’re going to talk about those guys in a while actually.
